stable.finish-args-host-os-ro-filesystem-access: COSMIC ships its keyboard shortcut defaults as a data file in /usr/share/cosmic on the host. Displaying the user's effective shortcuts is the entire purpose of this app, and Flatpak reserves /usr inside the sandbox, so read-only host-os access is the only way to read that file; XDG_DATA_DIRS is extended with /run/host/usr/share so the configuration library finds it at its host location. Without it the app could only show custom bindings and would be useless. Nothing on the host is written.
stable.finish-args-unnecessary-xdg-config-cosmi: The app registers its global shortcut by writing one entry into the COSMIC compositor's custom shortcut file under ~/.config/cosmic, which the compositor watches and reloads immediately. This is the same mechanism COSMIC Settings uses, and xdg-desktop-portal-cosmic has no GlobalShortcuts interface, so there is no portal alternative. The app only ever adds, updates or removes its own entry, re-reads the file immediately before writing, and refuses to write at all if any entry fails to parse, so other shortcuts cannot be lost.
stable.finish-args-flatpak-spawn-access: Rows in the cheatsheet can be clicked to run the shortcut they document, for example opening a terminal or the app library or changing the volume. Those commands come from the compositor's own system-action configuration and belong to the host session; they do not exist inside the sandbox. They are handed to flatpak-spawn --host so they run exactly as the compositor would run them. Only commands already configured in the user's COSMIC shortcut configuration are ever executed.
